analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) FX Trader Call Today, 2) Fed Call Change, 3) BRL Update, 4) Latest on El Nino and TTF and 5) Equities Update
key_insights: GS now expects a third 25bp Fed hike in March 2027, on top of the second 25bp hike still expected in December. A third hike could come in January, but March is judged more likely.

GS expects November and December inflation reports to be softer, then larger start-of-year price increases to lift January inflation. Inflation is still expected to be meaningfully lower by the end of 2027 as tariff, energy shock and AI price effects fade.
GS leaves its terminal fed funds forecast unchanged at 3.25-3.5%. It now expects cuts to start in December 2027 (previously September 2027), followed by cuts in March, June and September 2028.

GS expects most FOMC participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot. A firmer January inflation report would make delivering the hike the path of least resistance even if the energy shock appears over by then.

October core CPI rose 0.30%, above expectations, on firmer readings across a broad set of categories. Shelter was firm again, medical services were firm despite a decline in health insurance prices, and motor vehicle insurance rebounded.
From the CPI details GS estimates October core PCE rose 0.35% (vs 0.23% expected before CPI), or +3.30% y/y. It estimates headline PCE rose 0.36% in October, or 3.87% y/y.

GS reads the Copom minutes as broadly neutral with a dovish tilt. Copom attributes the worse inflation path mainly to first-round supply shocks it does not plan to react to, which suggests a high bar for near-term hikes.
GS expects Copom to stay on hold until at least 2Q27 and sees room for only limited cuts in 2027, with high uncertainty over growth, fiscal policy and the supply shocks.

USDBRL is back at post-election highs on a stronger USD, lower oil, unclear fiscal measures and a dovish BCB tone. GS EM FX strategy flags the risk that high rates cannot support BRL much further without a clearer fiscal anchor.

A possible fiscal adjustment would exclude certain revenues from the spending-growth calculation to meet 2027 targets. It falls short of a spending cut but may support BRL today after yesterday's selloff.

GS FX trading says USDBRL broke 5.53, tested the YTD highs and traded through 5.60 after the strong CPI, with CTA USD buying driving momentum. Offshore corporate USD supply appeared near 5.60, and GS sees around 5.60 as an OK sell, with resistance near 5.61.

Brazil DI rates closed the day sideways. The curve widened about 20bps from the day lows after US CPI, then trimmed losses on headlines that Fontelles would take the finance minister job if Lula invites him. Jan29 DIs held near 14.70.

NOAA estimates say the Super El Nino is here, but ECMWF long-range models still call for an average Nov-Mar winter across NW Europe. GS expects TTF to trade on Middle East escalation headlines and short-run weather models through year-end.

GS's 1Q27 TTF forecast is 74 EUR/MWh. It combines a 44 EUR estimated fair value with a 26/4 EUR supply/weather risk premium, and assumes Mideast LNG supply keeps improving (it averaged above 40% of pre-war levels over the past week).

GS European gas trading cites reports of Hormuz negotiations, possible talk of reopening Russian gas flows to Europe, and the earliest sudden stratospheric warming event seen, which could bring cold weather to Europe and Asia in early to mid December. Risk positions unwound and gas prices sold off.

GS equity flow desk says SPX barely fell on the hot CPI day and futures are recovering. VIX briefly traded into the 20s but finished below 20, and the market struggled to hold a volatility premium. It reads positioning as supporting the tape more than macro undermines it.

GS says gross exposure has been cut, nets are historically low and appetite to add risk has fallen substantially. It sees this as a tailwind for the tape, and expects the elevated volatility premium to keep decaying absent fresh negative news.

GS flags rates as a headwind but not yet flashing red, since yields need another leg higher before they become a material problem (rate of change matters). Credit is the one to watch, with high yield spreads chopping sideways. Higher oil, stickier inflation and a more hawkish Fed form a reflexive loop.

Neocloud commentary overnight was broadly supportive. Data centre capacity remains the main operational bottleneck and compute utilization is elevated. Market focus is on hardware delivery and developer coding workflows.

tension_points.bull_case: Cut gross exposure, historically low nets and heavy hedging mean positioning supports the tape, and the elevated volatility premium should keep decaying absent fresh negative information.
tension_points.bear_case: A more hawkish Fed, higher oil and stickier inflation, with yields needing only another leg higher to become a material problem for equities, and credit spreads as the one to watch.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields making another leg higher, or fresh negative information that stops the volatility premium from decaying.

tension_points.bull_case: Potential fiscal adjustment measures and offshore corporate USD supply near 5.60 could support BRL.
tension_points.bear_case: A dovish BCB tone, unclear fiscal measures, a stronger USD and CTA USD buying keep USDBRL near post-election highs, and an on-hold Copom would not necessarily support BRL.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained break above the 5.61 resistance.
